title: Reflection from a ferrite half-space biased in its surface
source: G. H. B. Thompson, J. Brit. IRE, June 1956, pp. 311-328, Eq. 13; resonance at 1 GHz and 4 pi Ms = 1000 G from J. D. Adam et al., Ch. 7 of Modern Ferrites Vol. 2 (IEEE/Wiley, 2023), Fig. 7.5
notes: Bias along +y (Euler [0, -90, 0] takes the principal z to y). At normal incidence the s wave (E along the bias, h across it) sees the extraordinary permeability mu_eff = (mu^2 - kappa^2) / mu (Thompson Eq. 13), and is totally reflected where a lossless mu_eff is negative. The p wave sees mu = 1. Values are Adam's: 1 GHz, 4 pi Ms = 1000 G; eps is chosen. The sweep is in frequency at a fixed internal field of 100 Oe.
